_provenance.what: The public human leaderboard arcprize.org serves for each ARC-3 game: the top 10 human runs by action count, as the site itself ranks them, for all 25 builds in current-builds.json plus as66-821a4dcad9c2. Alongside each game, the per-level baseline the site shows as the human average. These are NOT replays and this file is NOT a third replay manifest -- see the first caveat.
_provenance.why: published-replays.json carried a caveat asserting the blog's 250 guids were 'a curated best-of'. That was an inference from the list's shape, never a measurement, and it is wrong in the direction that matters: it made the blog set look like worse corpus input than it is. Correcting it needed a real best-of to compare against, and this is it. Committed rather than left in a chat message because the corrected caveat cites these numbers, and a citation to numbers nobody can re-read is not a correction.
_provenance.collected: 2026-09-15. Leaderboard rows: one POST https://arcprize.org/api/leaderboards/<4-char game id> per game, header Content-Type: application/json, body {"ai": false, "game_id": "<4-char id>"}. UNAUTHENTICATED -- no API key, no cookie, no session; anyone can re-run these 26 requests and get this file back. The 4-char id is the game_id up to the first hyphen, and all 26 ids were checked to be exactly 4 characters rather than assumed. baseline_actions is NOT from this endpoint: it is copied from the committed current-builds.json, which took it from an authenticated GET https://three.arcprize.org/api/games. It was cross-checked against the level_baseline_actions field of four /api/sessions run documents -- both of the Boss's g50t runs (guids 4f0689d0-7d06-4be7-91ac-31cb9a800b85 and 58483738-cfaf-4e57-8c55-4c9c593bbab5), his cn04 run f714032e-914d-4bb5-bc95-386dfacebca0 and his ft09 run 99084b22-7e67-4e13-8d68-6095e944255f -- and agrees element-for-element with all four. Nothing here was transcribed from a chat message or a doc.
caveats: A LEADERBOARD ROW IS NOT FETCHABLE AND WILL NEVER BE. It carries user_name and no guid -- the six fields are user_name, end_state, score, actions, resets, published_at, and that is the whole row. Without a guid there is no /api/sessions document and no /api/recordings download, so these 250 runs are permanently visible-but-unreachable. Nobody should later try to label them, join them to either replay manifest by id, or treat this file as a source of episodes. It is a reference measurement and nothing else. scripts/test_decision_step_validator.py asserts that no row here carries a guid, so the day the endpoint starts returning one, the suite says so instead of the assumption quietly going stale.

baseline_total_actions IS A PER-GAME CONSTANT, NOT A PER-RUN FIGURE. It is the sum of baseline_actions, which the API reports per level for the build, identical for every run on that build regardless of who played it or how they did. The check that establishes this rather than assuming it: the Boss played g50t-5849a774 twice, on 13-Sep and 15-Sep, and both session documents report level_baseline_actions [78,175,179,230,96,54,67] -- the same seven numbers, summing to 879 -- while his own level_actions differed on all seven levels. Do not read it as anything any particular player did.

as66-821a4dcad9c2 RETURNS ZERO LEADERBOARD ROWS while all 25 current builds return exactly 10. The request succeeds -- HTTP 200, a well-formed JSON array -- and the array is empty. Recorded as observed. Nothing here establishes WHY, and this file does not guess: no-qualifying-runs, cleared-with-the-game, and never-populated are all consistent with an empty array. It is an independent data point on the game's absence from the lineup, not an explanation of it. See docs/trace-findings/2026-09-15-as66-the-withdrawn-26th-game.md. as66 also has no baseline_actions here, because it is absent from current-builds.json, which is this file's only source for that field.

EVERY ONE of the 250 rows is end_state WIN with score exactly 100. Resets are non-zero on only 24 of them and never exceed 6. That uniformity is the point of the file: it is what a genuine best-of looks like, and it is what published-replays.json's 250 rows (139 WIN, 70 GAME_OVER, 41 NOT_FINISHED, resets to 30) demonstrably are not.

These rows and published-replays.json's rows are disjoint sets, established by timestamp rather than by id, because there is no id. Every row in published-replays.json carries published_at 2026-03-22; these run 2026-04-14 to 2026-09-11 and not one is 2026-03-22. That holds across all 25 games at once. Per-game action ranges do NOT establish it -- they are disjoint on g50t, cd82 and lp85 but overlap on bp35, ft09 and sb26.

Only 10 of published-replays.json's 25 game_ids are still in the live lineup, so a blog-versus-leaderboard comparison is only legitimate on those 10; on the other 15 the leaderboard is serving a different build of the game. The 4-char leaderboard id has no build component at all, which means this endpoint gives you whatever build it currently considers that game -- it cannot be asked for a historical build, and this file is therefore a snapshot with the same expiry as current-builds.json.

Ranking and pagination were not probed. The rows arrive sorted by ascending actions and the file preserves that order verbatim, but nothing was checked about whether 10 is a cap, a page, or all there is. The {"ai": false} body field implies an {"ai": true} counterpart; it was not requested, and no claim is made about it.

fields.game_id: the full build id from current-builds.json; as66 is the one entry not from that file
fields.leaderboard_id: the 4-char id the endpoint takes -- game_id up to the first hyphen
fields.baseline_total_actions: sum of baseline_actions; a per-GAME constant, null for as66
fields.baseline_actions: per-level baseline from current-builds.json; null for as66
fields.row_count: rows the endpoint returned -- 10 for every current build, 0 for as66
fields.rows[].user_name: the display name the leaderboard shows; there is NO guid beside it
